issues.description: lean_plan preregistered 'E(z)^2 > 0 for 0<Om<1, z>-1 (any real w)'. The delivered theorems assume z >= 0, a strictly narrower domain (still covering every data redshift and the whole prior box). The stronger z > -1 version is true and would prove with the same tactic (linarith on 1+z>0). Not a correctness problem; a small unflagged departure from the preregistered statement.

I re-ran the Elenchus ledger gate read-only: rc=1 with 0 blocks and exactly the 6 unaudited-Tier-A flags, as reported. The rows correctly keep audit: null. This referee pass audited all six statements (see lean_statement_audit); a later stage may fill the audit objects citing this review, which would bring the gate to rc=0 without fabricating anything.

The byline 'Generated with Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5), model-assisted, human-supervised' names a model version that is not recorded anywhere in the artifacts and asserts human supervision that nothing in results/ documents. Either drop the model name and the supervision claim or cite a log that supports them; as written it is an unverifiable provenance statement in an otherwise fully provenance-tracked paper.

NC5 passes its preregistered criterion (median PTE 3.4e-6 < 1e-3), but 6 of the 20 individual scrambled-covariance fits give PTE > 1e-3 (seeds 202: 0.022, 208: 0.080, 210: 0.067, 212: 0.0088, 215: 0.0034, 218: 0.0070). The control therefore has limited per-realisation discriminating power; the paper reports only the median and should say that a scrambled covariance is often still an acceptable fit, so this control mainly tests the covariance ordering in aggregate.

CLAUDE.md requires `python antigravity_guard.py` to pass before work is called done; it exits 1 with 54 findings, one of which is this stage's scripts/desi_dr2_bao/dr2_model.py (import of fit_desi_bao via a sys.path insert). The other 53 are pre-existing. Disclosed in the stage notes; still an open repo-level gate for this deliverable.

My isolated re-run (copies of scripts/ under /tmp/ref_dr2_rerun, worktree outputs untouched) reproduced controls.json and camb_crosscheck.json bit-for-bit, and the DR2_LCDM, DR2_wCDM and DR1_LCDM chains bit-identically (np.array_equal true; these three chains carry all four scored targets, r, and the DR1->DR2 shift). The LCDM grid runs printed in the re-run log match grid_summary.json/fit.json exactly (e.g. DR2_LCDM grid mean 0.2978258521000865 / 101.52332484000979). The DR1_wCDM and two radiation chains and the 141^3 wCDM grids were still running when this report was forced out, so those report-only numbers (DR1 wCDM instrument check, radiation shifts, wCDM grid moments) are verified from the committed chain files and log lines but not from a completed regeneration.

issues.description: The paper says the DR1 wCDM h r_d = 101.7 (+2.9/-3.5) Mpc value was 'not re-fetched for this paper'. I re-fetched arXiv:2404.03002v3 p.36 via alphaXiv and it reads r_d h = (101.7 +2.9 -3.5) Mpc (wCDM), so the caveat can be closed. Likewise all four DR2 targets (eq. 17: 0.2975+-0.0086, 101.54+-0.73, r=-0.92; Table V wCDM 'DESI': 0.2969+-0.0089, w=-0.916+-0.078), chi2/dof = 10.2/(13-2), the 'Table 2 of [38]' prior sentence, 2404.03002 eq. 4.1/5.1 and its Table 2 priors U[0.01,0.99], U[10,1000], U[-3,1] were re-fetched and match the preregistration exactly; the DR2 file means match Table IV v3 to rounding and the file DM-DH correlations differ from Table IV by +0.069 (LRG3+ELG1) and +0.036 (ELG2) as the caveat states. No sign of post-hoc target tuning: preregistration.json (15:55:09 UTC, sha256 723cd27d...32a4) predates every script (15:58+) and every output.

lean_statement_audit.comment: Statement: 0<Om, Om<1, 0<=z, any real w -> 0 < Om*(1+z)^3 + (1-Om)*(1+z)^(3*(1+w)) with a genuine Real.rpow exponent. Matches dr2_model.e_of_z with orad=0 (numpy zp1**(3*(1+w))). Hypotheses strictly contain the sampler's prior box Om in (0.01,0.99), w in [-3,1], and every data redshift. Non-vacuous (E2 is a transparent def, not an opaque constant). Only gap: preregistered domain was z > -1; delivered z >= 0.

E := Real.sqrt E2; with E2 > 0 the conclusion 0 < E is the real content (Real.sqrt of a non-positive would be 0, so the statement is not trivially true). Correctly supports well-definedness of 1/E on the prior box.

For all Om, z: E Om (-1) z = ANSE.BAOFlatLCDM.E Om z, where the parent def is Real.sqrt (Om*(1+z)^3 + (1-Om)) (BAO_FlatLCDM.lean line 24). Proof reduces (1+z)^(0:R)=1 via Real.rpow_zero, valid for every real base, so the universal quantification is legitimate. Exactly the nesting used to call LCDM the w=-1 special case of the wCDM fit.

StrictMonoOn (E Om w) (Ici 0) under 0<Om<1 and -1 <= w. Hypothesis w >= -1 is sufficient, not necessary (E is still increasing for mildly phantom w when Om is not tiny), and the docstring honestly says no claim is made for w < -1. Covers the DR2 best fit w ~ -0.916. Non-vacuous.

ContinuousOn (fun t => (E Om w t)^-1) (Ici 0) for 0<Om<1 and every real w. Uses rpow_const continuity with base 1+t >= 1 > 0 and non-vanishing from E_pos. Exactly the regularity needed for the comoving-distance integrand; no trivialising hypothesis.

Dc Om w z := intervalIntegral of (E Om w t)^-1 over 0..z; theorem: StrictMonoOn on Ici 0 for 0<Om<1 and EVERY real w. Because a Mathlib interval integral of a non-integrable function is 0, the statement would be false if integrability were not established, so the result is substantive (it proves IntervalIntegrable via continuity and uses intervalIntegral_pos_of_pos_on). Faithful to D_C = int_0^z dt/E(t) in predict_quad/predict_gl up to the c/100 prefactor and 1/(h r_d) normalisation, which the docstring states. Nothing is claimed about quadrature accuracy, which is correct.
